audit_status.source_base: Hebrew 1 Samuel chapter 22, first-pass restored draft
audit_status.review_note: Reviewed for cave refugee community, debt and distress, Moabite refuge, Saul's patronage/conspiracy speech, Ahimelech's defense, refusal of royal guards, Doeg's role and ethnicity, priest massacre, destruction of Nob including infants and animals, Abiathar's survival, and David's responsibility statement.

verses.restored: David went from there and escaped to cave of Adullam. His brothers and all house of his father heard and went down to him there.

familiar.text: David therefore departed thence, and escaped to the cave Adullam: and when his brethren and all his father’s house heard it, they went down thither to him.

modern.text: So David left Gath and took refuge in the cave of Adullam. When his brothers and the rest of his father’s household heard about it, they went down to him there.

original.text: וַיֵּ֤לֶךְ דָּוִד֙ מִשָּׁ֔ם וַיִּמָּלֵ֖ט אֶל מְעָרַ֣ת עֲדֻלָּ֑ם וַיִּשְׁמְע֤וּ אֶחָיו֙ וְכָל בֵּ֣ית אָבִ֔יו וַיֵּרְד֥וּ אֵלָ֖יו שָֽׁמָּה

verses.restored: Every distressed person, everyone who had a creditor, and everyone bitter of life gathered to him, and he became commander over them. About four hundred men were with him.

familiar.text: And every one that was in distress, and every one that was in debt, and every one that was discontented, gathered themselves unto him; and he became a captain over them: and there were with him about four hundred men.

modern.text: And all who were distressed or indebted or discontented rallied around him, and he became their leader. About four hundred men were with him.

original.text: וַיִּֽתְקַבְּצ֣וּ אֵ֠לָיו כָּל אִ֨ישׁ מָצ֜וֹק וְכָל אִ֨ישׁ אֲשֶׁר ל֤וֹ נֹשֶׁא֙ וְכָל אִ֣ישׁ מַר נֶ֔פֶשׁ וַיְהִ֥י עֲלֵיהֶ֖ם לְשָׂ֑ר וַיִּהְי֣וּ עִמּ֔וֹ כְּאַרְבַּ֥ע מֵא֖וֹת אִֽישׁ

verses.restored: David went from there to Mizpeh of Moab and said to king of Moab, Please let my father and my mother go out with you until I know what Divine will do for me.

familiar.text: And David went thence to Mizpeh of Moab: and he said unto the king of Moab, Let my father and my mother, I pray thee, come forth, and be with you, till I know what God will do for me.

modern.text: From there David went to Mizpeh of Moab, where he said to the king of Moab, “Please let my father and mother stay with you until I learn what God will do for me.”

original.text: וַיֵּ֧לֶךְ דָּוִ֛ד מִשָּׁ֖ם מִצְפֵּ֣ה מוֹאָ֑ב וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֶל מֶ֣לֶךְ מוֹאָ֗ב יֵֽצֵא נָ֞א אָבִ֤י וְאִמִּי֙ אִתְּכֶ֔ם עַ֚ד אֲשֶׁ֣ר אֵדַ֔ע מַה יַּֽעֲשֶׂה לִּ֖י אֱלֹהִֽים

verses.restored: He brought them before king of Moab, and they stayed with him all days David was in stronghold.

familiar.text: And he brought them before the king of Moab: and they dwelt with him all the while that David was in the hold.

modern.text: So he left them in the care of the king of Moab, and they stayed with him the whole time David was in the stronghold.

original.text: וַיַּנְחֵ֕ם אֶת פְּנֵ֖י מֶ֣לֶךְ מוֹאָ֑ב וַיֵּשְׁב֣וּ עִמּ֔וֹ כָּל יְמֵ֥י הֱיוֹת דָּוִ֖ד בַּמְּצוּדָֽה

verses.restored: Gad the prophet said to David, Do not stay in stronghold. Go and enter land of Judah. David went and came to forest of Hereth.

familiar.text: And the prophet Gad said unto David, Abide not in the hold; depart, and get thee into the land of Judah. Then David departed, and came into the forest of Hareth.

modern.text: Then the prophet Gad said to David, “Do not stay in the stronghold. Depart and go into the land of Judah.” So David left and went to the forest of Hereth. Saul Slays the Priests of Nob (Psalms 52:1–9)

original.text: וַיֹּאמֶר֩ גָּ֨ד הַנָּבִ֜יא אֶל דָּוִ֗ד לֹ֤א תֵשֵׁב֙ בַּמְּצוּדָ֔ה לֵ֥ךְ וּבָֽאתָ לְּךָ֖ אֶ֣רֶץ יְהוּדָ֑ה וַיֵּ֣לֶךְ דָּוִ֔ד וַיָּבֹ֖א יַ֥עַר חָֽרֶת

verses.restored: Saul heard that David and men with him had been discovered. Saul was sitting in Gibeah under tamarisk on height, spear in his hand, and all his servants standing around him.

familiar.text: When Saul heard that David was discovered, and the men that were with him, (now Saul abode in Gibeah under a tree in Ramah, having his spear in his hand, and all his servants were standing about him;)

modern.text: Soon Saul learned that David and his men had been discovered. At that time Saul was in Gibeah, sitting under the tamarisk tree on the hill at Gibeah, with his spear in hand and all his servants standing around him.

original.text: וַיִּשְׁמַ֣ע שָׁא֔וּל כִּ֚י נוֹדַ֣ע דָּוִ֔ד וַאֲנָשִׁ֖ים אֲשֶׁ֣ר אִתּ֑וֹ וְשָׁאוּל֩ יוֹשֵׁ֨ב בַּגִּבְעָ֜ה תַּֽחַת הָאֶ֤שֶׁל בָּֽרָמָה֙ וַחֲנִית֣וֹ בְיָד֔וֹ וְכָל עֲבָדָ֖יו נִצָּבִ֥ים עָלָֽיו

verses.restored: Saul said to servants standing around him, Hear, please, Benjaminites! Will son of Jesse give all of you fields and vineyards? Will he set all of you as commanders of thousands and commanders of hundreds?

familiar.text: Then Saul said unto his servants that stood about him, Hear now, ye Benjamites; will the son of Jesse give every one of you fields and vineyards, and make you all captains of thousands, and captains of hundreds;

modern.text: Then Saul said to his servants, “Listen, men of Benjamin! Is the son of Jesse giving all of you fields and vineyards and making you commanders of thousands or hundreds?

original.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר שָׁא֗וּל לַֽעֲבָדָיו֙ הַנִּצָּבִ֣ים עָלָ֔יו שִׁמְעוּ נָ֖א בְּנֵ֣י יְמִינִ֑י גַּם לְכֻלְּכֶ֗ם יִתֵּ֤ן בֶּן יִשַׁי֙ שָׂד֣וֹת וּכְרָמִ֔ים לְכֻלְּכֶ֣ם יָשִׂ֔ים שָׂרֵ֥י אֲלָפִ֖ים וְשָׂרֵ֥י מֵאֽוֹת

verses.restored: For all of you have conspired against me, and no one uncovers my ear when my son cuts covenant with son of Jesse. None of you grieves for me or uncovers my ear that my son has raised my servant against me as one lying in wait, as this day.

familiar.text: That all of you have conspired against me, and there is none that sheweth me that my son hath made a league with the son of Jesse, and there is none of you that is sorry for me, or sheweth unto me that my son hath stirred up my servant against me, to lie in wait, as at this day?

modern.text: Is that why all of you have conspired against me? Not one of you told me that my own son had made a covenant with the son of Jesse. Not one of you has shown concern for me or revealed to me that my son has stirred up my own servant to lie in wait against me, as is the case today.”

original.text: כִּי֩ קְשַׁרְתֶּ֨ם כֻּלְּכֶ֜ם עָלַ֗י וְאֵין גֹּלֶ֤ה אֶת אָזְנִי֙ בִּכְרָת בְּנִ֣י עִם בֶּן יִשַׁ֔י וְאֵין חֹלֶ֥ה מִכֶּ֛ם עָלַ֖י וְגֹלֶ֣ה אֶת אָזְנִ֑י כִּ֣י הֵקִים֩ בְּנִ֨י אֶת עַבְדִּ֥י עָלַ֛י לְאֹרֵ֖ב כַּיּ֥וֹם הַזֶּֽה

verses.restored: Doeg the Edomite, stationed over servants of Saul, answered and said, I saw son of Jesse coming to Nob, to Ahimelech son of Ahitub.

familiar.text: Then answered Doeg the Edomite, which was set over the servants of Saul, and said, I saw the son of Jesse coming to Nob, to Ahimelech the son of Ahitub.

modern.text: But Doeg the Edomite, who had stationed himself with Saul’s servants, answered: “I saw the son of Jesse come to Ahimelech son of Ahitub at Nob.

original.text: וַיַּ֜עַן דֹּאֵ֣ג הָאֲדֹמִ֗י וְה֛וּא נִצָּ֥ב עַל עַבְדֵֽי שָׁא֖וּל וַיֹּאמַ֑ר רָאִ֨יתִי֙ אֶת בֶּן יִשַׁ֔י בָּ֣א נֹ֔בֶה אֶל אֲחִימֶ֖לֶךְ בֶּן אֲחִטֽוּב

verses.restored: He inquired of YHWH for him, gave him provisions, and gave him sword of Goliath the Philistine.

familiar.text: And he enquired of the LORD for him, and gave him victuals, and gave him the sword of Goliath the Philistine.

modern.text: Ahimelech inquired of the LORD for him and gave him provisions. He also gave him the sword of Goliath the Philistine.”

original.text: וַיִּשְׁאַל לוֹ֙ בַּֽיהוָ֔ה וְצֵידָ֖ה נָ֣תַן ל֑וֹ וְאֵ֗ת חֶ֛רֶב גָּלְיָ֥ת הַפְּלִשְׁתִּ֖י נָ֥תַן לֽוֹ

verses.restored: King sent to call Ahimelech the priest son of Ahitub and all house of his father, priests who were in Nob. All of them came to king.

familiar.text: Then the king sent to call Ahimelech the priest, the son of Ahitub, and all his father’s house, the priests that were in Nob: and they came all of them to the king.

modern.text: Then the king sent messengers to summon Ahimelech the priest, the son of Ahitub, and his father’s whole family, who were priests at Nob. And all of them came to the king.

original.text: וַיִּשְׁלַ֣ח הַמֶּ֡לֶךְ לִקְרֹא֩ אֶת אֲחִימֶ֨לֶךְ בֶּן אֲחִיט֜וּב הַכֹּהֵ֗ן וְאֵ֨ת כָּל בֵּ֥ית אָבִ֛יו הַכֹּהֲנִ֖ים אֲשֶׁ֣ר בְּנֹ֑ב וַיָּבֹ֥אוּ כֻלָּ֖ם אֶל הַמֶּֽלֶךְ

verses.restored: Saul said, Hear, please, son of Ahitub. He said, Here I am, my lord.

familiar.text: And Saul said, Hear now, thou son of Ahitub. And he answered, Here I am, my lord.

modern.text: “Listen now, son of Ahitub,” said Saul. “Here I am, my lord,” he replied.

original.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר שָׁא֔וּל שְֽׁמַֽע נָ֖א בֶּן אֲחִיט֑וּב וַיֹּ֖אמֶר הִנְנִ֥י אֲדֹנִֽי

verses.restored: Saul said to him, Why have you conspired against me, you and son of Jesse, by giving him bread and sword and inquiring of Divine for him, so he rose against me as one lying in wait, as this day?

familiar.text: And Saul said unto him, Why have ye conspired against me, thou and the son of Jesse, in that thou hast given him bread, and a sword, and hast enquired of God for him, that he should rise against me, to lie in wait, as at this day?

modern.text: And Saul asked him, “Why have you and the son of Jesse conspired against me? You gave him bread and a sword and inquired of God for him so that he could rise up against me to lie in wait, as he is doing today.”

original.text: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר אלו שָׁא֔וּל לָ֚מָּה קְשַׁרְתֶּ֣ם עָלַ֔י אַתָּ֖ה וּבֶן יִשָׁ֑י בְּתִתְּךָ֨ ל֜וֹ לֶ֣חֶם וְחֶ֗רֶב וְשָׁא֥וֹל לוֹ֙ בֵּֽאלֹהִ֔ים לָק֥וּם אֵלַ֛י לְאֹרֵ֖ב כַּיּ֥וֹם הַזֶּֽה

verses.restored: Ahimelech answered king and said, Who among all your servants is as faithful as David, son-in-law of king, captain over your guard, and honored in your house?

familiar.text: Then Ahimelech answered the king, and said, And who is so faithful among all thy servants as David, which is the king’s son in law, and goeth at thy bidding, and is honourable in thine house?

modern.text: Ahimelech answered the king, “Who among all your servants is as faithful as David, the king’s son-in-law, the captain of your bodyguard who is honored in your house?

original.text: וַיַּ֧עַן אֲחִימֶ֛לֶךְ אֶת הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ וַיֹּאמַ֑ר וּמִ֤י בְכָל עֲבָדֶ֨יךָ֙ כְּדָוִ֣ד נֶאֱמָ֔ן וַחֲתַ֥ן הַמֶּ֛לֶךְ וְסָ֥ר אֶל מִשְׁמַעְתֶּ֖ךָ וְנִכְבָּ֥ד בְּבֵיתֶֽךָ

verses.restored: Did I begin that day to inquire of Divine for him? Far be it from me! Let not king place anything against his servant or against all house of my father, for your servant knew nothing of all this, small or great.

familiar.text: Did I then begin to enquire of God for him? be it far from me: let not the king impute any thing unto his servant, nor to all the house of my father: for thy servant knew nothing of all this, less or more.

modern.text: Was that day the first time I inquired of God for him? Far be it from me! Let not the king accuse your servant or any of my father’s household, for your servant knew nothing of this whole affair—not in part or in whole.”

original.text: הַיּ֧וֹם הַחִלֹּ֛תִי לשאול ל֥וֹ בֵאלֹהִ֖ים חָלִ֣ילָה לִּ֑י אַל יָשֵׂם֩ הַמֶּ֨לֶךְ בְּעַבְדּ֤וֹ דָבָר֙ בְּכָל בֵּ֣ית אָבִ֔י כִּ֠י לֹֽא יָדַ֤ע עַבְדְּךָ֙ בְּכָל זֹ֔את דָּבָ֥ר קָטֹ֖ן א֥וֹ גָדֽוֹל

verses.restored: King said, Dying, you shall die, Ahimelech, you and all house of your father.

familiar.text: And the king said, Thou shalt surely die, Ahimelech, thou, and all thy father’s house.

modern.text: But the king replied, “You will surely die, Ahimelech, you and all your father’s house!”

original.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר הַמֶּ֔לֶךְ מ֥וֹת תָּמ֖וּת אֲחִימֶ֑לֶךְ אַתָּ֖ה וְכָל בֵּ֥ית אָבִֽיךָ

verses.restored: King said to runners stationed around him, Turn and put priests of YHWH to death, because their hand also is with David, and because they knew he was fleeing and did not uncover my ear. But servants of king were not willing to stretch out their hand to fall upon priests of YHWH.

familiar.text: And the king said unto the footmen that stood about him, Turn, and slay the priests of the LORD: because their hand also is with David, and because they knew when he fled, and did not shew it to me. But the servants of the king would not put forth their hand to fall upon the priests of the LORD.

modern.text: Then the king ordered the guards at his side, “Turn and kill the priests of the LORD, because they too sided with David. For they knew he was fleeing, but they did not tell me.” But the king’s servants would not lift a hand to strike the priests of the LORD.

original.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר הַמֶּ֡לֶךְ לָרָצִים֩ הַנִּצָּבִ֨ים עָלָ֜יו סֹ֥בּוּ וְהָמִ֣יתוּ כֹּהֲנֵ֣י יְהוָ֗ה כִּ֤י גַם יָדָם֙ עִם דָּוִ֔ד וְכִ֤י יָֽדְעוּ֙ כִּֽי בֹרֵ֣חַ ה֔וּא וְלֹ֥א גָל֖וּ אֶת אזנו וְלֹֽא אָב֞וּ עַבְדֵ֤י הַמֶּ֨לֶךְ֙ לִשְׁלֹ֣חַ אֶת יָדָ֔ם לִפְגֹ֖עַ בְּכֹהֲנֵ֥י יְהוָֽה

verses.restored: King said to Doeg, You turn and fall upon priests. Doeg the Edomite turned and fell upon priests. He put to death that day eighty-five men bearing linen ephod.

familiar.text: And the king said to Doeg, Turn thou, and fall upon the priests. And Doeg the Edomite turned, and he fell upon the priests, and slew on that day fourscore and five persons that did wear a linen ephod.

modern.text: So the king ordered Doeg, “You turn and strike down the priests!” And Doeg the Edomite turned and struck down the priests himself. On that day he killed eighty-five men who wore the linen ephod.

original.text: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר הַמֶּ֨לֶךְ֙ לדויג סֹ֣ב אַתָּ֔ה וּפְגַ֖ע בַּכֹּהֲנִ֑ים וַיִּסֹּ֞ב דויג הָאֲדֹמִ֗י וַיִּפְגַּע הוּא֙ בַּכֹּ֣הֲנִ֔ים וַיָּ֣מֶת בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֗וּא שְׁמֹנִ֤ים וַחֲמִשָּׁה֙ אִ֔ישׁ נֹשֵׂ֖א אֵפ֥וֹד בָּֽד

verses.restored: Nob, city of priests, he struck by mouth of sword: man and woman, child and nursing infant, ox and donkey and sheep, by mouth of sword.

familiar.text: And Nob, the city of the priests, smote he with the edge of the sword, both men and women, children and sucklings, and oxen, and asses, and sheep, with the edge of the sword.

modern.text: He also put to the sword Nob, the city of the priests, with its men and women, children and infants, oxen, donkeys, and sheep.

original.text: וְאֵ֨ת נֹ֤ב עִיר הַכֹּֽהֲנִים֙ הִכָּ֣ה לְפִי חֶ֔רֶב מֵאִישׁ֙ וְעַד אִשָּׁ֔ה מֵעוֹלֵ֖ל וְעַד יוֹנֵ֑ק וְשׁ֧וֹר וַחֲמ֛וֹר וָשֶׂ֖ה לְפִי חָֽרֶב

verses.restored: One son of Ahimelech son of Ahitub escaped, and his name was Abiathar. He fled after David.

familiar.text: And one of the sons of Ahimelech the son of Ahitub, named Abiathar, escaped, and fled after David.

modern.text: But one of the sons of Ahimelech son of Ahitub escaped. His name was Abiathar, and he fled to David.

original.text: וַיִּמָּלֵ֣ט בֵּן אֶחָ֗ד לַאֲחִימֶ֨לֶךְ֙ בֶּן אֲחִט֔וּב וּשְׁמ֖וֹ אֶבְיָתָ֑ר וַיִּבְרַ֖ח אַחֲרֵ֥י דָוִֽד

verses.restored: Abiathar told David that Saul had killed priests of YHWH.

familiar.text: And Abiathar shewed David that Saul had slain the LORD’s priests.

modern.text: And Abiathar told David that Saul had killed the priests of the LORD.

original.text: וַיַּגֵּ֥ד אֶבְיָתָ֖ר לְדָוִ֑ד כִּ֚י הָרַ֣ג שָׁא֔וּל אֵ֖ת כֹּהֲנֵ֥י יְהוָֽה

verses.restored: David said to Abiathar, I knew that day, because Doeg the Edomite was there, that telling, he would tell Saul. I have caused/occasioned death of every life of house of your father.

familiar.text: And David said unto Abiathar, I knew it that day, when Doeg the Edomite was there, that he would surely tell Saul: I have occasioned the death of all the persons of thy father’s house.

modern.text: Then David said to Abiathar, “I knew that Doeg the Edomite was there that day, and that he was sure to tell Saul. I myself am responsible for the lives of everyone in your father’s house.

original.text: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר דָּוִ֜ד לְאֶבְיָתָ֗ר יָדַ֜עְתִּי בַּיּ֤וֹם הַהוּא֙ כִּֽי שָׁם֙ דויג הָאֲדֹמִ֔י כִּֽי הַגֵּ֥ד יַגִּ֖יד לְשָׁא֑וּל אָנֹכִ֣י סַבֹּ֔תִי בְּכָל נֶ֖פֶשׁ בֵּ֥ית אָבִֽיךָ

verses.restored: Stay with me; do not fear. For whoever seeks my life seeks your life, but with me you are under guard.

familiar.text: Abide thou with me, fear not: for he that seeketh my life seeketh thy life: but with me thou shalt be in safeguard.

modern.text: Stay with me; do not be afraid, for he who seeks your life is seeking mine as well. You will be safe with me.”

original.text: שְׁבָ֤ה אִתִּי֙ אַל תִּירָ֔א כִּ֛י אֲשֶׁר יְבַקֵּ֥שׁ אֶת נַפְשִׁ֖י יְבַקֵּ֣שׁ אֶת נַפְשֶׁ֑ךָ כִּֽי מִשְׁמֶ֥רֶת אַתָּ֖ה עִמָּדִֽי

translation_notes: The cave community gathers people in distress, debt, and bitterness. Poverty, indebtedness, displacement, and trauma do not make people criminal or disposable.
David becomes commander of a vulnerable armed group. Refugee leadership requires accountability and does not sanctify everything the group later does.
David seeks safety for his parents in Moab. Cross-border refuge and kinship ties complicate any simple enemy map.
Saul appeals to patronage, tribal loyalty, grievance, and conspiracy. Leaders often turn personal fear into accusations against whole networks.
Saul's repeated 'son of Jesse' rhetoric reduces David's identity and stokes factional contempt; it must not become a political slur.
Ahimelech gives a truthful defense based on David's known royal status. He is not responsible for David's deception or Saul's violence.
Saul orders an extrajudicial mass execution. The royal servants' refusal is morally significant: subordinates may refuse an unlawful command.
Doeg carries out the killing, but his Edomite identity does not cause it. Ethnicity must never be used to explain cruelty or condemn a people.
The eighty-five priests, women, men, children, nursing infants, and animals of Nob are victims of a state massacre. The text must not be sanitized as judgment or collateral damage.
David acknowledges causal responsibility in exposing the household, but Saul and Doeg remain responsible for choosing massacre. Survivor guilt must not absorb perpetrator guilt.
Abiathar is a survivor of family and community annihilation. His later role does not erase trauma or make survival evidence of special favor.
safety_note: Maximum safeguards: Nob is a clerical and civilian massacre ordered by Saul and carried out by Doeg. It must never be defended as national security, obedience, punishment for association, or acceptable collateral damage. Children, infants, animals, priests, and residents are not combatants. Doeg's ethnicity is irrelevant to moral blame. The servants' refusal to kill shows that unjust orders may and should be resisted. David's regret does not transfer Saul's and Doeg's guilt onto a survivor or refugee community.
